 The FDA Approved a New Sunscreen Ingredient for the First Time in Decades—Here’s What We Thought 
 Follow Beauty & Personal Care View feed The FDA Approved a New Sunscreen Ingredient for the First Time in Decades—Here’s What We Thought 
 We tested four new formulas with the new filter to see how they compare.
 By Danusia Wnek Published: Oct 27, 2026 Save Article Share Article Good Housekeeping/ Danusia Wnek We've been independently researching and testing products for over 120 years. If you buy through our links, we may earn a commission. Learn more about our review process. 
 3 min read This summer marked a major milestone for the sunscreen industry. For the first time in over two decades, the Food and Drug Administration ( FDA ) approved a new UV filter for use in sunscreens in the United States called bemotrizinol , or BEMT. After the 60 day waiting period for the Final Order to take effect, BEMT sunscreens are slowly hitting shelves, with four new launches from three brands: Ultra Violette, Neutrogena, and La Roche-Posay.
 As a Senior Chemist at the Good Housekeeping Institute Beauty Lab , I’ve tested hundreds of sunscreen formulas over the past decade. BEMT has been widely used in sunscreens in Europe, Asia, and Australia for years so I was beyond excited to try these new launches.
 We tried the new BEMT sunscreens
 Good Housekeeping/ Danusia Wnek Ultra Violette Unblock Screen SPF 50 Sunscreen was the first BEMT sunscreen to hit shelves. At SPF 50, it is one of the lower SPF values among the new launches I tried. It differs from the others as the only tinted option, combines BEMT with a mineral sunscreen active, and comes in a pump packaging. It has a mousse-like texture and a matte finish that is very reminiscent of mineral sunscreens, which I think would make this great for combo/ oily skin. The tint is very sheer on on my light skin tone.
 Ultra Violette Unblock Screen SPF 50 Sunscreen
 Ultra Violette Unblock Screen SPF 50 Sunscreen
 $40 Sephora SPF Value 50 
 Active ingredients Bemotrizinol 3%,
Octocrylene 6%, 
Zinc Oxide 10% 
 Water resistance No 
 Price per ounce $23.5 
 Neutrogena Ultra Sheer Daily Face Sunscreen has the highest SPF value of the BEMT sunscreens I tried, at SPF 70. This lightweight fluid absorbs quickly and leaves a soft, almost powdery feel. It doesn’t feel greasy and provides a smooth base for my everyday medium coverage foundation. Overall, I think it would be a great option for normal to oily skin.
 Neutrogena Ultra Sheer Daily Face Sunscreen Broad Spectrum SPF 70
 Neutrogena Ultra Sheer Daily Face Sunscreen Broad Spectrum SPF 70
 $17 Amazon Also Consider $20 Ulta Beauty SPF Value 70 
 Active Ingredients Avobenzone (3%), Bemotrizinol (6%), Homosalate (15%), Octisalate (5%) 
 Water resistance No 
 Price per ounce $12.1 
 Neutrogena Clear Face Acne Prone Skin Broad Spectrum SPF 60 applies easily onto skin and feels like a lightweight lotion. It’s a little more hydrating than Ultra Sheer and doesn’t have the powdery feel. Although it claims to be “formulated for acne prone skin,” I think most skin types looking for lightweight hydration may enjoy it too.
 Neutrogena Clear Face Sunscreen Acne-Prone Skin Broad Spectrum SPF 60

 Active Ingredients Avobenzone (3%), Bemotrizinol (6%), Homosalate (15%), Octisalate (5%)

 La Roche-Posay Anthelios UVDefense Sunscreen SPF 50 has one of the lower SPF values in the group. When dispensed, it has a fluid texture similar to the two Neutrogena formulas. I was pleasantly surprised how quickly this lotion soaked into my skin, leaving it comfortably hydrated with a silky-smooth finish.

Octisalate (5%)
Octocrylene (6%)

 Price per ounce $23.5 
 The bottom line
 For years, other countries have had access to newer UV filters, while US options remained limited due to FDA regulations. After more than 20 years, formulators now have a new ingredient to create more modern, innovative formulas.
 After trying all four launches, I found that they’re all lightweight and absorb quickly sans the greasiness sometimes associated with chemical sunscreens. The non-tinted options didn’t have a noticeable white cast, as chemical sunscreens generally don’t. All four are face sunscreens that are not water resistant, making them a good fit for daily use. I’m looking forward to see BEMT slowly roll into body and water-resistant formulas, too.
 Why trust Good Housekeeping?
 Good Housekeeping Senior Chemist Danusia Wnek has evaluated hundreds of sunscreens for the face and body for more than a decade. For this article, she personally tried all the new BEMT formulas and shared her firsthand impressions.
